JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KRISHNA S.DIXIT  AND  THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL)

These appeals have been filed by the claimants seeking for enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the common judgment and award dated 01.12.2018 passed in MVC.No.892/2017 and 893/2017 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Ranebennur.

2. Brief facts leading to filing of these appeals are that on 01.04.2017 the deceased Sri. Honnappa Karimallappanavar and deceased Smt. Nanda were proceeding on Hero Honda Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-27-R-3015 at that time bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 34-F-1015 owned by the respondent Corporation driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle which resulted in accident.
It is averred that the rider and pillion rider sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to those injuries.

The dependants have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V.
Act before the Tribunal seeking for compensation.

3. Respondent-Corporation entered appearance, opposed the claim petition by filing objection and denied occurrence of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:13049-DB accident due to the negligence of the driver,
age, income and avocation of the deceased.
The Tribunal recorded the evidence of parties and the claimants examined themselves as PW1 and PW2 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P21.
Respondent examined RW1 to RW3 and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R6.

The Tribunal in MVC No.892/2017 has awarded total compensation of Rs.11,95,052/- and in MVC No.893/2017 has awarded total compensation Rs. 9,69,000/- along with the interest at the rate of 7% per annum.

Being aggrieved,
these appeals have been filed seeking for higher compensation.

3

4. Sri. G.S. Hulmani, learned counsel appearing for the appellants submits that in both the judgment and awards the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income and further committed an error in not awarding compensation on the head of future prospects and awarding meager compensation on all other heads.
Hence, he seeks to allow both the appeals.

5. Per contra, Sri. S.C. Bhuti, learned counsel appearing for the Corporation supports the impugned judgment and awards of the Tribunal and submits that the Tribunal has justified in assessing the income as the appellants failed to produce any proof of evidence with regard to the income.
It is submitted that in MFA No.101161/2019 the appellants are mother in law and husband of the deceased.
The mother-in law cannot be considered as the dependent.

Hence, the NC:
2024:KHC-D:13049-DB appropriate deduction will be 50%.
Hence, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
6. We have heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
7. It is not in dispute that in a road accident dated 01.04.2017 one Sri. Honnapa Karimallappanavar and Smt. Nanda sustained grievous Injuries and succumbed to those injuries.
It is also not in dispute that the accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus owned by the respondent Corporation.
In MFA.No.101161/2019 (MVC 893/2017) the deceased was aged about 20 years at the time of accident.
Admittedly, the claimants have not produced any cogent and acceptable evidence to prove the income.
Hence, the income of the deceased is notionally reassessed at Rs. 10,250/- per month placing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the KSLSA.
The appellants are entitled to an addition of 40% of the assessed income towards loss of future prospects.
There is no dispute with regard to the multiplier of 18 and appropriate deduction would be 1/3 towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased.
The contention of the Corporation is that one of the claimant i.e., mother-in-law cannot be considered as dependant.
The said contention is taken note for the purpose of rejection only.
The material on record indicates that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:13049-DB mother-in-law of the deceased was residing with the deceased and was dependent on the deceased.

8. Further, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.44,000/- each under the head of loss of consortium, besides Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,5000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses including 10% escalation and the entire compensation is reassessed as under:
Loss of dependency (10,250+40% x12x18x2/3) Rs.20,66,400/-

Loss of consortium Rs. 88,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs. 16,500/-
 Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-
